ranking.candidate: exact-revision online FP8 on L40S via the actual pinned-vLLM producer/consumer
why_now: It is the only retained representation whose producer can start from the exact BF16 revision at runtime; it does not depend on an unbound community checkpoint.
Its missing decision fact is actual pinned-consumer time at the exact six stock Gemma shapes, not another endpoint controller or 62.5-GB checkpoint transfer.
L40S planning cost is 33.8% of H200 planning cost, so a slower service can still win the same whole-request market target.
Existing generic FP8 CUDA evidence is encouraging but invalid for the exact consumer/shape claim, making this a short, high-information correction rather than duplicated readiness work.
ranking.hypothesis: At the maximum logically fitting online-FP8 concurrency, actual pinned-vLLM FP8 transformer linears, actual FP8 KV writer, and the BF16 tied head leave positive room under the 1.394581-second planning-base whole-service ceiling for attention and scheduler overhead.

capacity_prior.interpretation: c12 is the robust point; c14 is allocator-sensitive but logically fits; c15 is outside the envelope. The 10K c1 logical total is 39.935866 GiB. These are capacity priors, not runtime allocations.

first_scientific_arm.proven_lifecycle: reuse the lifecycle path that produced gemma_l40s_parallel_lm_head_measurement_final; use one lowercase RFC-1123 allocation and no project-specific readiness/controller successor
first_scientific_arm.checkpoint: forbidden; create deterministic synthetic BF16 weights one exact shape at a time and let Fp8LinearMethod's online producer prepare the consumed weights
first_scientific_arm.actual_consumer: vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8.Fp8LinearMethod create_weights/process_weights_after_loading/apply, plus the actual pinned-vLLM FP8 KV-cache writer; matched actual BF16 linear and BF16 ParallelLMHead consumers are comparators
first_scientific_arm.measurement: Warmup then raw CUDA-event and synchronized wall distributions. Architecture-weight actual rows by layer multiplicity. Measure prefill work per request without dividing it by decode concurrency, decode work per request at m=12/m=14, the actual head, and actual FP8 KV writes. Require finite outputs and a small BF16 numerical oracle that consumes timed outputs. Preserve GPU identity, allocator peaks, power/utilization interval, concrete classes, and source hashes.
first_scientific_arm.whole_request_decision: Add only disjoint measured components. Do not double-count the head or KV writer and do not call an omitted attention/scheduler residual a pass. Compare the component lower bound with both L40S service ceilings.
first_scientific_arm.comparator: Same L40S, shapes, activations, order randomization, repetitions, BF16 source weights, and actual BF16 linear/head consumers. Production quality comparator remains the exact BF16 checkpoint at the same revision/tokenizer/prompts, not the synthetic oracle.
first_scientific_arm.quality_boundary: This component arm establishes only runnable mechanism and numerical sanity. An endpoint is admissible only after the component lower bound leaves positive planning margin; production requires raw exact-revision 4214/358 and 10K captures, local/global probes, stop/parser/logprob behavior, failures/reloads, and a sealed scorer against BF16.
first_scientific_arm.scientific_stop_rule: Typed negative if any required actual consumer cannot execute, any required row is missing/nonfinite, online production and timed consumption are disconnected, c12 and c14 both exceed the planning-base service ceiling before attention/scheduler, or c14 allocator peak exceeds the 44.704-GiB envelope. A valid positive only admits one later exact endpoint; it does not establish economics or quality.
first_scientific_arm.pre_science_stop_rule: If the exact image cannot import the already resolved concrete classes or the proven lifecycle fails before a GPU row, emit a typed operational failure, clean up, and do not repair or relaunch in this project.

prospective_budget.storage: one 100-GiB provider boot disk; 512 MiB retained artifacts plus 2 GiB temporary

ranking.promotion_trigger: FP8_COMPONENT_ADMISSION: all required actual rows are valid, c12 or c14 logically fits measured allocator telemetry, and the disjoint measured component sum is below the 1.394581-second planning ceiling with a positive named residual for attention/scheduler. Then and only then consider one exact online-FP8 endpoint owner.

ranking.candidate: W4 Marlin on L40S as a semantics-changing exact-shape mechanism proxy
ranking.why_not_primary: W4 has much better derived decode and capacity margins, but no candidate binds the exact base revision and immutable producer/calibration inputs. It cannot outrank exact-revision online FP8 until the actual Marlin advantage is large enough to justify creating and quality-testing an exact producer.
ranking.trigger: W4_RESIDUAL_TRIGGER: the primary emits a valid scientific terminal and online FP8 either exceeds the planning ceiling or leaves less than 0.35 seconds/request for attention plus scheduler at its best fitting point; the W4 program is already staged, can start within ten minutes, and the retained owner has at least ten provider minutes remaining. A strong FP8 pass, invalid FP8 terminal, missed deadline, or unready W4 program forces immediate teardown.
ranking.first_scientific_arm: In the same exact-image L40S session and sequential owner, invoke actual AWQMarlinLinearMethod on the same six shapes at m=14 and m=16 using deterministic synthetic group-128 asymmetric packed W4 weights and a dequantized BF16 oracle. Measure actual CUDA/wall distributions and architecture-weighted prefill/decode components; retain the BF16 tied head and the same FP8-KV contract.
ranking.comparator: Matched actual online FP8 primary and BF16 consumers from the same session; no checkpoint or endpoint.
ranking.quality_boundary: This is explicitly a semantics-changing synthetic mechanism proxy. It is not deployable until an exact-revision, content-addressed producer is created and representative raw outputs/features pass the exact quality consumer against BF16.
ranking.scientific_stop_rule: Close W4 if any actual Marlin row is invalid, if its architecture-weighted component time is less than 20% better than matched online FP8, or if the c16 disjoint component floor exceeds 0.60 seconds/request. Passing only justifies exact-producer work; it does not justify a W4 endpoint.

rejected_or_deferred.reason: The official assistant is only 0.875 GiB and the acceptance gate is explicit, but useful benefit depends on measured decode fraction and accepted-token rate. Prompt-prefill dominates this workload, and the first acceptance result requires the exact target plus assistant endpoint/checkpoint rather than a checkpoint-free component. Reopen only behind an already resident exact endpoint and require >=5% all-in gain with exact greedy output IDs.

Public exact-model support is a useful prior and prior paid failures were pre-science, not a negative. The immutable H100 command fails static capacity before KV, and the H200 route's next result requires another full checkpoint endpoint after repeated pre-GPU program failures. It violates this successor's direct-mechanism criterion.

H100 saves only 13.8% versus H200 at planning rates, while the exact BF16 route is capacity-limited to lower concurrency and has no scope-matched component evidence showing it can recover that gap. Its next credible result is checkpoint-first.

Its $0.77/h public rate and SM89/96-MB-L2 geometry are attractive, but throughput and sustained placement are unmeasured. It is eligible only after the L40S actual Marlin mechanism passes, and then needs a matched component/workload result and current written committed quote.
Official support and $2.60/h planning price are priors only; no immutable ROCm image or executable self-service venue is bound. The next action would be access/runtime binding rather than science.

FP8_BLOCK lacks exact base revision and its pinned SM89 consumer is unsupported; W4 lacks exact base revision and immutable producer/calibration provenance. Neither should trigger a checkpoint transfer before the actual-consumer mechanism passes.
